title.value: Dynamic Demonstrations Controller for In-Context Learning

abstract.value: In-Context Learning (ICL) is a new paradigm for natural language processing (NLP), where a large language model (LLM) observes a small number of demonstrations and a test instance as its input, and directly makes predictions without updating model parameters. Previous studies have revealed that ICL is sensitive to the selection and the order of demonstrations. However, there are few studies regarding the impact of the demonstration number on the ICL performance within a limited input length of LLM, because it is commonly believed that the number of demonstrations is positively correlated with model performance. In this paper, we find this conclusion does not always hold true. Through pilot experiments, we discover that increasing the number of demonstrations does not necessarily lead to improved performance. Building upon this insight, we propose a $\textbf{D}$ynamic $\textbf{D}$emonstrations $\textbf{Controller}$ $({\textbf{D$^2$Controller}})$, which can improve the ICL performance by adjusting the number of demonstrations dynamically. The experimental results show that D$^2$Controller yields a 5.4\% relative improvement on eight different sizes of LLMs across ten datasets. Moreover, we also extend our method to previous ICL models and achieve competitive results.
